mainTopic: Lashes for an oath broken by doing nothing, how to treat two conflicting סתם משניות, and whose view the first משנה of שבועות follows.
overview: This amud opens with the end of a later משנה (דף כז:). That משנה says a שבועת ביטוי brings מלקות when broken on purpose and a קרבן עולה ויורד when broken by mistake. From the word "this", the גמרא learns that swearing "I will eat" and then not eating brings no מלקות, which supports רבי יוחנן. The גמרא asks why we should follow this סתם משנה over the first משנה (דף ב.). It answers that רבי changed his mind: the later משנה is his final view, and the earlier one stayed because a משנה does not move from its place. The גמרא then goes back to its earlier reading of the first משנה as רבי ישמעאל and talking about מלקות. It defends that reading for נגעים and for carrying on שבת, but finally drops it because of the משנה's own words: "two that are four", forgetting in between, and a קרבן עולה ויורד. רב יוסף then explains that רבי followed רבי ישמעאל for ידיעות and רבי עקיבא for שבועות. רב כהנא adds that רבי holds these views for his own reasons, and he begins to prove it from a ברייתא where רבי disagrees with רבי עקיבא's source. That proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The later משנה: lashes for intentional violation, an offering for unwitting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ending of the later משנה (דף כז:). Repeating the same oath makes him liable only once. A שבועת ביטוי carries מלקות if broken on purpose and a קרבן עולה ויורד if broken by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is liable only once. This is the oath on an utterance: if he breaks it on purpose, he gets lashes, and if he breaks it by mistake, he brings an offering that goes up or down depending on what he can afford.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is quoting the end of a later משנה, which it is about to use as a source for רבי יוחנן's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case in this משנה is a negative oath ("I will not eat this loaf") that was repeated, so the second oath adds nothing and he is liable once. The key line is the closing summary: this kind of oath brings מלקות on purpose and a קרבן עולה ויורד by mistake. The next step will squeeze an inference out of the word "this" (זו).

keyTerms.meaning: An oath someone says about himself, such as "I will eat" or "I will not eat"
Its intentional violation
Its unwitting (mistaken) violation
Lashes (מלקות) given by a בית דין
A sliding-scale offering: a rich person brings an animal, a poorer person brings birds or flour

phrases.english: he is liable for only one.
phrases.notes: This is the end of a later משנה (דף כז:) about someone who repeated the same oath.

phrases.english: This is the oath on an utterance,
for which one is liable to lashes for its intentional violation,
and for its unwitting violation, a sliding-scale offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ הִיא שְׁבוּעַת בִּיטּוּי, שֶׁחַיָּיבִין עַל זְדוֹנָהּ מַכּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quotation of the later משנה, which the גמרא brings as a possible source for רבי יוחנן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שבועת ביטוי carries מלקות for intentional violation and a קרבן עולה ויורד for unwitting violation; a repeated identical oath creates only one liability.

steps.title: Inference: "I will eat" and not eating brings no lashes
steps.stepSummary: From the word "this" (זו), the גמרא infers that only this kind of case (where he actually ate) gets מלקות. Swearing "I will eat" and then not eating gets no מלקות, which supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: "This is the one for which one gets lashes for breaking it on purpose." That means if he said "I will eat" and did not eat, he is not lashed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely to prove רבי יוחנן's ruling: breaking an oath by doing nothing does not bring מלקות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's case involves eating, which is a real action. By saying "this is" the oath that brings מלקות, the משנה implies that other cases do not. The case left out is "I will eat" followed by not eating, where no action was done, so no מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: "This is": read as "only this case," which leaves other cases out
But (here it brings in the case that is excluded)
He is not lashed

steps.whyThisMatters: This backs the well-known rule that one generally gets no מלקות for a לאו שאין בו מעשה, a prohibition broken without any action.

phrases.english: "This is the one for which one is liable to lashes for its intentional violation":
but if he swore "I will eat" and did not eat,
he is not lashed!

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ הִיא דְּחַיָּיבִין עַל זְדוֹנָהּ מַכּוֹת – אֲבָל אוֹכַל וְלֹא אָכַל, לָא לָקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the משנה quoted in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's ruling that one who swore "I will eat" and did not eat gets no מלקות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The later משנה (דף כז:), read from the word "זו הִיא" (this is) to mean only cases like it.

steps.title: Why follow this unattributed משנה over the other one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects. The earlier משנה (דף ב.) is also a סתם משנה, and it seems to treat "I will eat" like the other oaths. Why did רבי יוחנן choose to follow this one?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, this one is an unattributed משנה and that one is an unattributed משנה. What did he see that made him act according to this unattributed משנה? Let him act according to that unattributed משנה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's choice of source: there are two unattributed משניות that point in different directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סתם משנה normally carries weight as the accepted ruling. Here each משנה is a סתם, and they seem to disagree about "I will eat" and not eating. Nothing obvious makes one stronger, so picking the later one looks arbitrary.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, after all (opens a point that both sides already accept)
An unattributed (anonymous) משנה, which normally sets the accepted ruling
What did he see? Why choose this?
Let him act (according to)

steps.confusionAlert: Both "הַאי סְתָמָא" phrases look identical, but they point to different משניות. The one he followed is the later משנה (דף כז:), and the one he could have followed is the first משנה (דף ב.).

phrases.english: Now, this is an unattributed Mishnah and that is an unattributed Mishnah;
phrases.notes: One is the later משנה just quoted (דף כז:); the other is the first משנה of the מסכתא (דף ב.).

phrases.aramaic: מַאי חָזֵי דְּעָבֵיד כִּי הַאי סְתָמָא?
phrases.english: what did he see that he acts in accordance with this unattributed Mishnah?
Let him act in accordance with that unattributed Mishnah!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof from step 2 by pointing to an equally authoritative unattributed משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's reliance on the later משנה (דף כז:) as the source for his ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two סתם משניות carry equal weight. If they conflict, there is no clear reason to prefer the later one over the earlier one (דף ב.).

steps.title: How could רבי himself set down two conflicting unattributed rulings?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further: "by your reasoning" that the two are equal, how could רבי, who arranged the משנה, record one view anonymously here and the opposite view anonymously there? The next step answers this.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning: רבי himself, how could he teach us anonymously one way here and another way there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the problem around: the conflict is not only רבי יוחנן's problem but רבי's. This sets up an explanation that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "ולטעמיך" means the challenger's own assumption leads to a bigger problem. If both סתם משניות are equal and conflicting, then רבי produced a contradiction in the משנה. That cannot be right, so there must be a way to explain which סתם reflects the final ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning: turns the questioner's own assumption against him
Himself
He taught us anonymously (recorded a view without a name)

steps.whyThisMatters: This raises a general question about how to handle two anonymous משניות that seem to conflict, a question that comes up across ש״ס.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning:
Rebbi himself,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא, the one who put the משנה together.

phrases.english: how could he teach us anonymously
here this way and there that way?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ – רַבִּי גּוּפֵיהּ, הֵיכִי סְתַם לַן הָכָא הָכִי וְהָכָא הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to step 3 by showing that its premise makes רבי himself contradictory. This prepares an explanation of how the two סתם משניות relate.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption from step 3 that the two סתם משניות are equal and conflicting.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both anonymous rulings carry equal weight and disagree, then רבי recorded a contradiction. That is impossible, so there must be an explanation that reconciles them or ranks one above the other.

steps.title: רבי changed his mind, but the first משנה stayed in place
steps.stepSummary: At first רבי held that one gets מלקות for a לאו with no action and taught it anonymously. Later he held that one does not, and taught that anonymously too. The first משנה was not erased, because a משנה does not move from its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, at first רבי held that a person gets lashes for a prohibition that involves no action, and he taught it as an anonymous משנה. Then he changed his mind and held that one does not get lashes for it, and he taught that as an anonymous משנה too. The earlier משנה was left where it was, because a משנה does not move from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4: the two anonymous משניות are not equal, because one is רבי's earlier view and the other is his later view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swearing "I will eat" and then not eating is a לאו שאין בו מעשה, because the person did nothing. The משנה on דף ב. reflects רבי's first opinion (lashes), and the משנה on דף כז: reflects his final opinion (no lashes). That is why רבי יוחנן follows the later one.

keyTerms.meaning: A Torah prohibition that is broken without doing any action
He taught it anonymously, as a סתם משנה with no name attached
And then he changed his mind and held
A משנה does not move from its place. Once it was taught, it was not removed.

steps.whatToRemember: The two סתם משניות are not a contradiction. The משנה on דף ב. is רבי's first view, and the משנה on דף כז: is his final view. רבי יוחנן follows the final one: no מלקות for a לאו with no action.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the earlier משנה is still the הלכה just because it still appears in the text. It stayed only because a משנה, once taught, was not taken out.

phrases.english: Rather, at first he held

phrases.aramaic: לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה לוֹקִין עָלָיו, וְסַתְמַהּ,
phrases.english: that for a prohibition with no action one gets lashes, and he taught it anonymously,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר סָבַר אֵין לוֹקִין עָלָיו, וְסַתְמַהּ;
phrases.english: and then he changed his mind and held that one does not get lashes for it, and he taught that anonymously;
and a משנה does not move from its place.
phrases.notes: Once students had learned the first משנה, it was left in the text even after רבי changed his view.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 about two opposite סתם משניות
steps.terutzResolutionType: Chronological: an earlier view and a later retraction
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two סתם משניות look equal, so there seems to be no reason to prefer one
steps.terutzMaskana: The later משנה is רבי's final view. The earlier one stayed only because a משנה is not removed.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a general tool for two anonymous משניות that contradict each other: one can be the author's earlier view and the other his later view.

steps.title: If the first משנה is about lashes, where are the lashes for נגעים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא recalls that it explained the first משנה as following רבי ישמעאל and talking about מלקות. It then asks what מלקות could exist in the list of מראות נגעים.
steps.simpleTranslation: How did you explain the משנה? As following רבי ישמעאל, and as talking about lashes. But for the shades of נגעים, what lashes are there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its earlier reading of the משנה on דף ב. and tests it. If the whole משנה is about lashes, then the list of נגעים must also have a lashes case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first משנה gives several parallel lists: oaths, ידיעות, יציאות שבת and מראות נגעים. If the counting means "cases of מלקות", every list needs a lashes case. A נגע is about טומאה, so it is unclear where lashes would come in.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you explain it? (literally: in what did you set it?)
Lashes given by בית דין
The shades of צרעת marks

phrases.english: How did you explain it?
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier discussion, where the first משנה was explained this way.

phrases.english: As following רבי ישמעאל, and as talking about lashes;
the shades of נגעים: what lashes are there?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי יוחנן discussion and returns to test the earlier reading of the first משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the משנה on דף ב. as following רבי ישמעאל and being about מלקות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every list in the משנה must then involve lashes, but the laws of נגעים don't seem to have any lashes case

steps.title: Lashes for cutting off a נגע
steps.stepSummary: Lashes apply to someone who cuts off his בהרת. This follows רבי אבין in the name of רבי אילעא: wherever the Torah says השמר, פן or אל, it is a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is where he cuts off his בהרת, following רבי אבין in the name of רבי אילעא. For רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אילעא: wherever it says "השמר", "פן" or "אל", it is nothing other than a לא תעשה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds a lashes case for נגעים: cutting off the mark.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah says "השמר בנגע הצרעת" (be careful with the נגע). By רבי אילעא's rule, the word השמר makes this a לא תעשה. So cutting off the בהרת breaks a לאו and brings מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Cuts off his בהרת, the white צרעת mark
"Be careful", "lest", "do not": words that signal a prohibition
A negative commandment (a לאו)

phrases.english: Where he cuts off his בהרת,
and following רבי אבין, who said in the name of רבי אילעא;

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אָבִין אָמַר רַבִּי אִילְעָא:
phrases.english: for רבי אבין said in the name of רבי אילעא:
wherever it says "be careful," "lest," or "do not,"
phrases.notes: For נגעים the פסוק is דברים 24:8, "השמר בנגע הצרעת".

phrases.english: it is nothing other than a prohibition.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a specific case that carries lashes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There seemed to be no לאו with lashes in the laws of נגעים
steps.terutzMaskana: Cutting off a בהרת breaks a לאו, based on the word השמר, and brings מלקות
steps.whyThisMatters: רבי אילעא's rule that השמר, פן and אל signal a לאו is used all over ש"ס.

steps.title: Where are the lashes for carrying on שבת?
steps.stepSummary: Carrying out on שבת is a לאו that carries a court death penalty, and normally there are no מלקות for such a לאו. So how can this list be about lashes?
steps.simpleTranslation: Carrying out on שבת: what lashes are there? It is a prohibition that serves as the warning for a court death penalty, and for any such prohibition one does not get lashes!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the next list in the first משנה, carrying out on שבת, and asks where lashes could apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking שבת on purpose is punished with death by בית דין. The usual rule is that a לאו whose punishment is a court death penalty does not bring lashes. So the lashes reading seems to fail here.

keyTerms.meaning: Carrying objects out from one domain to another on שבת

keyTerms.term: לָאו שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְאַזְהָרַת מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין
keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition that serves as the warning for a death penalty given by בית דין

phrases.english: Carrying out on שבת: what lashes are there?

phrases.aramaic: לָאו שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְאַזְהָרַת מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין הוּא –
phrases.english: It is a prohibition given as a warning for a court death penalty,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל לָאו שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְאַזְהָרַת מִיתַת בֵּית דִּין,
phrases.english: and any prohibition given as a warning for a court death penalty,
one does not get lashes for it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After נגעים was answered, this is a parallel challenge on the next list
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the list of יציאות שבת in the first משנה is about lashes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A לאו that carries a court death penalty does not bring lashes, so carrying on שבת should have no lashes case

steps.title: That is exactly why we said רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that this is the very reason it explained the משנה as רבי ישמעאל, who holds that one does get lashes for a לאו that carries a court death penalty.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why we explained it as following רבי ישמעאל, who says: for a prohibition given as a warning for a court death penalty, one does get lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the question has no force, because רבי ישמעאל disagrees with the rule it was based on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule "no lashes for a לאו carrying a death penalty" is not held by everyone. רבי ישמעאל gives lashes for such a לאו, for example when the death penalty is not actually carried out. So carrying on שבת can have lashes according to him.

keyTerms.meaning: For that reason
We are explaining it (setting the משנה) as following

phrases.english: That is why we explain it
as following רבי ישמעאל, who says:

phrases.aramaic: לָאו שֶׁנִּיתַּן לְאַזְהָרַת מִיתַת בֵּית דִין –
phrases.english: for a prohibition given as a warning for a court death penalty,
one does get lashes for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם הָכִי קָא מוֹקֵימְנָא כְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about carrying on שבת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Pointing to a תנא who rejects the rule behind the question
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No one gives lashes for a לאו that carries a court death penalty
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי ישמעאל does give lashes for such a לאו, so the reading holds

steps.title: Could the משנה otherwise follow רבי עקיבא? The ידיעות list is a problem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does that mean that without this reason the משנה could follow רבי עקיבא? But the list of ידיעות would then be a problem for רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean that if not for this, it could stand as following רבי עקיבא? But the ידיעות are a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up on the wording of step 9, which implies that רבי ישמעאל was chosen only because of שבת. It challenges that implication.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 implied that רבי עקיבא would have worked if not for the שבת problem. But the ידיעות list in the first משנה, about forgetting טומאה or the מקדש, seemed to fit only רבי ישמעאל. So how could רבי עקיבא ever have been an option?

keyTerms.meaning: Does that mean that if not for this reason
The list in the משנה about being aware and then forgetting טומאה or the מקדש

phrases.english: Does that mean that if not for this,
it could stand as following רבי עקיבא?!
But the ידיעות are a difficulty!
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא does not count forgetting that it was the מקדש, while the משנה's list seems to count it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָאו הָכִי, קָיְימָא כְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.kashyaTarget: The implication that the משנה could follow רבי עקיבא if not for the שבת issue
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ידיעות list in the משנה doesn't fit רבי עקיבא's view, so he should never have been an option

steps.title: רבי עקיבא also works if the משנה is about lashes
steps.stepSummary: Just as the משנה was read as רבי ישמעאל talking about lashes, it can also be read as רבי עקיבא talking about lashes. That removes the ידיעות problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: Didn't you say it is רבי ישמעאל, and it is about lashes? So it can also be רבי עקיבא, and about lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the same move that saved רבי ישמעאל also saves רבי עקיבא: read the משנה as being about lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's limit on ידיעות is about when one brings a קרבן. If the משנה's counting is about מלקות, that limit doesn't matter. So the only real reason not to say רבי עקיבא is the שבת issue, just as step 9 implied.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't you say?
Also

steps.whatToRemember: The first משנה is read as being about מלקות. Both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא could fit the ידיעות list that way. רבי ישמעאל is chosen only because he gives lashes for carrying on שבת.

phrases.english: Didn't you say:
it is רבי ישמעאל, and it is about lashes?
It can also be רבי עקיבא, and about lashes.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אָמְרַתְּ: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל הִיא וּלְמַלְקוּת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the same reading (lashes) to the other תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ידיעות list rules out רבי עקיבא
steps.terutzMaskana: Read as being about lashes, the ידיעות list fits רבי עקיבא too. Only the שבת issue forces רבי ישמעאל.

steps.title: If the list is about lashes, why does it say awareness?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה is about מלקות, it should have used the word התראות (warnings), not ידיעות (awareness).
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say "awareness"? It should have said "warnings"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea from Steps 9-11 that the משנה is talking about lashes. It points to the משנה's own wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ידיעות fits the world of קרבנות, where a person sinned without knowing and later found out. For מלקות, the key condition is a התראה, a warning given before the sin. So a list about lashes should be called התראות.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if what you just said is true
Cases of awareness, when the person knows or finds out about the sin
Warnings given before a sin; needed before a court can give lashes
It should have said

phrases.english: If so, why does it say "awareness"?!
phrases.notes: "If so" means: if the משנה really is about lashes, as Step 11 said.

phrases.english: It should have said "warnings"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the lashes reading that Step 11 had just used to make the משנה fit רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the משנה as being about מלקות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Lashes depend on a warning, not on awareness, so the word ידיעות does not fit a lashes reading.

steps.title: Read it as awareness that comes from warnings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording slightly: read it as ידיעות דהתראות, the awareness that comes through warnings.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. Teach it as: "awareness of warnings."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the wording problem by adjusting how the משנה is read. It keeps the lashes reading alive for now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning is exactly what makes the person aware of the sin. So "awareness" can mean the awareness created by the warning, and the word ידיעות can stay.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not a difficulty
Awareness that comes from warnings

phrases.english: This is not difficult;
teach it as: "awareness of warnings."
phrases.notes: The גמרא is adjusting the wording, so read the משנה as meaning the awareness a person gets from being warned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of Step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word ידיעות proves the משנה is not about lashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: ידיעות can mean the awareness that comes from warnings, so the wording still fits lashes.

steps.title: Three reasons the lashes reading cannot work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings three proofs from the משנה that it cannot be about lashes: the count of four, the lapse of awareness, and the mention of a קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does it say "two that are four"? There are only two! And also, the case "where there was awareness at the beginning and awareness at the end and forgetting in between": what does forgetting have to do with lashes? And also, it says "this person brings a sliding-scale offering"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the lashes reading again, this time with three strong questions. Together they bring the whole lashes reading down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First, a person who was warned knows everything, so the four versions of forgetting cannot happen; there are only two cases (entering the מקדש and eating קדשים while טמא). Second, the משנה talks about forgetting in the middle, which matters only for קרבנות, not for lashes. Third, the משנה plainly ends with a קרבן עולה ויורד, so it is clearly about a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Two that are four; two basic cases that split into four
And furthermore; another question
Forgetting; a lapse of awareness
Lashes given by a court
A sliding-scale קרבן, whose cost depends on the person's wealth

steps.whatToRemember: The lashes reading is now dropped. The משנה is about קרבנות, so the problem of fitting both רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא comes back.

phrases.english: If so, why "two that are four"?!
They are only two!
phrases.notes: Someone who was warned is fully aware, so there are no forgetting versions; only the two basic cases are left.

phrases.english: And furthermore, "a case where there is awareness at the beginning
and awareness at the end, and forgetting in between" –
what does forgetting have to do with lashes?
And furthermore, "this one brings a sliding-scale offering"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, ״שְׁתַּיִם שֶׁהֵן אַרְבַּע״?! תַּרְתֵּי הוּא דְּהָוְיָין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 13 fixed the wording, this step brings three new problems that end the lashes reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the משנה as being about מלקות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The count of four, the forgetting in the middle, and the קרבן עולה ויורד all only make sense if the משנה is about קרבנות.

steps.title: רב יוסף: רבי followed different תנאים in different parts
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the משנה is רבי's. He followed רבי ישמעאל for the ידיעות part and רבי עקיבא for the שבועות part.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: It is רבי, and he arranged it following different תנאים. For awareness, he arranged it like רבי ישמעאל; for oaths, he arranged it like רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the lashes reading is gone, the גמרא gives a new answer to the old problem. One half of the משנה fits only רבי ישמעאל and the other half fits only רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, we tried to make the whole משנה fit one תנא. רב יוסף says that is not needed: רבי, who arranged the משנה, chose the view of a different תנא for each topic. So the משנה does not have to match one opinion all the way through.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; dropping the earlier approach for a new one
He took it up; he arranged it
Following different תנאים
Oaths

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף's answer: one משנה can follow רבי ישמעאל in one part and רבי עקיבא in another, because רבי arranged it that way.

phrases.english: Rather, רב יוסף said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי הִיא, וְנָסֵיב לַהּ אַלִּיבָּא דְתַנָּאֵי.
phrases.english: It is רבי, and he arranged it following different תנאים.
For awareness, he arranged it like רבי ישמעאל;
for oaths, he arranged it like רבי עקיבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: רַבִּי הִיא, וְנָסֵיב לַהּ אַלִּיבָּא דְתַנָּאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 14 ended the lashes reading, this gives a brand-new answer to the ידיעות/שבועות problem from Step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Split authorship: different parts of the משנה follow different תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole משנה must follow one תנא, so it can fit neither רבי ישמעאל nor רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי arranged the ידיעות part like רבי ישמעאל and the שבועות part like רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: רב כהנא: do not think רבי himself did not agree
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports that רב כהנא said not to understand רב יוסף as meaning that רבי only quoted these views without holding them himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I said this teaching in front of רב כהנא, and he said to me: Do not say that רבי arranged it following different תנאים but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי reports how רב כהנא reacted to רב יוסף's answer. רב כהנא rules out one way of understanding it, and this sets up his own explanation, which comes in step 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think רבי was just collecting other people's views. רב כהנא says that is wrong: the views in this משנה are not just quotes. His full point, how רבי himself holds, continues in the next line of the גמרא.

keyTerms.meaning: I said the teaching
In front of him
Do not say
He does not hold that way

steps.confusionAlert: רב כהנא is not rejecting רב יוסף's answer that the parts follow different תנאים. He is only rejecting the idea that רבי did not agree with them himself.

phrases.english: רב אשי said: I said this teaching
phrases.notes: "This teaching" is רב יוסף's answer from Step 15.

phrases.english: in front of רב כהנא,
and he said to me: Do not say
that רבי arranged it following different תנאים –
but he himself does not hold that way;
phrases.notes: The sentence keeps going in the next line, where רב כהנא explains what he does mean.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַמְרִיתָא לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows how רב יוסף's answer in Step 15 should be understood.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only one way of understanding רב יוסף's answer, not the answer itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The idea that רבי quoted these views without holding them himself

steps.title: רבי explains his own reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא says that רבי holds these views because of his own reasoning, not just because he is quoting others.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי is explaining his own reason.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא finishes the point from step 16. He says that רבי really holds these views and has his own reason for them. This line sets up a ברייתא that will show that reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16 רב כהנא said not to read רב יוסף as if רבי was only quoting רבי ישמעאל and רבי עקיבא. Now he gives the positive side: רבי has his own logic and his own source. The ברייתא that comes next is the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: his own reason
explains
rather (bringing in the correct way to understand it)

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi is explaining his own reasoning,
phrases.notes: This is still רב כהנא talking. רבי here means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who arranged the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the positive side of רב כהנא's correction in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי truly holds the views written in the משנה, and he has his own reasons for them.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns the rule from the word 'concealed' written twice
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that רבי עקיבא learns the need for awareness at the beginning and at the end from ונעלם, which the Torah writes twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: From where do we know that a person is liable only if he knew at the beginning, knew at the end, and forgot in between? The Torah says 'and it was concealed' and 'and it was concealed', two times. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב כהנא. First it shows רבי עקיבא's source for the rule that a person needs awareness at the beginning and at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bringing a קרבן עולה ויורד for טומאה needs three stages: knowing first, forgetting while sinning, and knowing again afterward. רבי עקיבא gets this from the extra ונעלם. One mention teaches that the person forgot, and the second mention teaches that he must have known before. The ברייתא will next show that רבי has his own, different source.

keyTerms.meaning: awareness at the beginning, before the sin
awareness at the end, after the sin
forgetting in between, at the time of the sin
'and it was concealed', the word in the פסוק
the פסוק teaches

steps.whyThisMatters: This three-stage rule is what the משנה means by 'ידיעות', so the source for it is central to the whole סוגיא.

phrases.english: As it is taught: From where do we know that he is liable
phrases.notes: He is liable to bring a קרבן עולה ויורד for entering the מקדש or eating קדשים while טמא.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא עַל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהּ יְדִיעָה בַּתְּחִלָּה
phrases.english: only for a case that has awareness at the beginning
and awareness at the end, and a lapse of awareness in between?
The verse says: 'And it was concealed,' 'and it was concealed,' two times,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that proves רב כהנא's claim.
steps.raayaObject: רב כהנא's claim that the positions in the משנה are רבי's own view, with his own reasoning, and not just views he quoted from other תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that records רבי עקיבא's source and then רבי's separate source.

steps.title: רבי says that proof is not needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי says רבי עקיבא's proof is unnecessary and begins to quote his own פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: That is not needed, because the פסוק says:
steps.whatsHappening: רבי disagrees with how רבי עקיבא learns the rule and starts to bring his own source. This line sets up the next step, where his פסוק is quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי agrees with the rule itself, but not with where רבי עקיבא learns it from. Because he has his own separate source, we see that he holds the rule for his own reasons. That is exactly what רב כהנא said.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not needed
for it says (bringing in a פסוק)

steps.confusionAlert: In this line רבי does not reject the rule of awareness at the beginning and at the end. He only says רבי עקיבא's proof from the double ונעלם is not needed. What רבי does with that extra word, and how it shows his own view, comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabbi says: It is not necessary,
phrases.notes: He means that רבי עקיבא's proof from the double ונעלם is not needed.

phrases.english: for it says:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Inside the ברייתא, רבי pushes aside רבי עקיבא's source and begins to offer his own.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי holds there is a different, simpler source for the three-stage awareness rule, and its פסוק is quoted next.
